algorithm: Server-side HTML rendering of a metrics table

classes.desc: Serves the dashboard HTML page and a JSON metrics endpoint.
classes.name: DashboardHandler

complexity: O(n) to render n metric rows
data_flow_ascii:
seeded RNG -> metric_rows -> render_page (HTML)
Browser/urllib GET / -> DashboardHandler -> HTML table
GET /api/metrics -> DashboardHandler -> JSON
description_sentence: Serves a single-page HTML dashboard of topic metrics plus a JSON metrics endpoint.
failure_note: Unknown paths return plain-text 404. The self-test asserts the title and row counts, printing FAILED if anything mismatches.

functions.desc: Render the full dashboard HTML page.
functions.name: render_page

functions.desc: Bind a ThreadingHTTPServer on 127.0.0.1 and serve it in a thread.
functions.name: start_server

functions.desc: Fetch the page and metrics endpoint; print a verification summary.
functions.name: run_self_test

functions.desc: Parse args; self-test by default or serve with --serve.
functions.name: main

label: Web dashboard
output_shape: Status lines for GET / and GET /api/metrics, a five-row metric sample, and a SELF-TEST PASSED/FAILED line.
pitch_sentence: A zero-dependency {topic} dashboard that renders live metrics as HTML and JSON, verified end to end by its own self-test.

qa.a: No; the table is rendered server-side as plain HTML, with a meta refresh tag for periodic updates.
A seeded RNG generates deterministic synthetic rows, so the dashboard is reproducible without any external data source.
qa.q: Where do the metrics come from?

qa.a: Yes, pass --serve to keep the ThreadingHTTPServer running on 127.0.0.1 until interrupted.

resume_bullet_template: Built a {topic} web dashboard in Python (stdlib http.server) rendering a server-side HTML metrics table with a JSON API; default run self-tests both endpoints on 127.0.0.1 and prints verification results.
run_notes: Add --serve to keep the dashboard running instead of self-testing.
scaling_note: Single-process threaded server rendering small pages; fine for local demos, not for high-traffic or large metric sets.
storage_note: No persistence: metrics are regenerated deterministically from the seed on every request and every run.
tradeoff_note: Plain HTML with no JS framework keeps it dependency-free but offers no interactivity beyond the auto-refresh meta tag.
